rationale: Lens: scope and split honesty, round 3 at 4c46cf64, re-read from disk. My three round-2 minor asks are all ADDRESSED in the diff: #251 is named with its boundary in Provenance, R4.2 and AC-11 (iii-neg) and its remainder routed to 130; 129b is five deliverables in Provenance, Non-Goals and OQ-1 alike; ADR-0045 Decision 5 now carries a transition clause and the ADR-0044 back-pointer names the target (`panel brief` template, specs 130–131) and the removal point (step 7). The `git diff cb272d50 4c46cf64` regression check in this lens is clean: the 129/129b/130 boundary still sits at a real seam, every new in-scope surface (readiness `Signal.Failures` API, R1.8's dispatch-into-T, the reattest caveats, the historical_skills snapshot) is priced in In Scope and Impacted Domains, core remains genuinely unchanged (R1.1 consumes `phase.FindEpicForBead` as-is; the waist tolerates `phase.Cache`'s explicit `-n 0`), and the one place 129 behaviour now reaches a terminal mutation verb (R4.3's set semantics inside `FindLandedMerge` reaching `complete`'s merged-unclosed reconcile) is stated with a safety argument and pinned by AC-12 (vii) rather than slipped in. Attacking the new selection rule: it cannot select another spec's bead (the ID must be `<E>.<N>` AND lineage must resolve to E; a `<E2>.<N>` bead with a `[S]` title fails the ID test, a `<E>.<N>` bead whose edge or title points elsewhere is N2, and R1.8 (a)/(b) refuse on every claim path), and the title fallback's failure modes (Sscanf of the first bracket, first epic with that spec_num) can only produce a false near-miss, never a false member. It CAN select a non-claimable bead: a follow-up `bd create --parent E` bug is plan-form by bd's ID scheme, so it is a member, and MF-1 then refuses it by name — the same as today, so not a regression, but OQ-7's rationale implies such follow-ups are informational near-misses when the common `--parent`-created one is a member; the spec should say so in one sentence and one AC leg. That is the only ask. #255, #239 and #232 remain fully homed; S0's deferral stands.
concrete_changes_required: State the member-but-not-claimable case explicitly: a bd-ready `<E>.<N>` bead with lineage E that has no `## Bead N` plan section (the common follow-up filed with `bd create --parent E`, which bd gives a plan-form ID regardless of issue_type) IS an R1.1 member, is excluded from R1.4's lifecycle tally when non-lifecycle, and is refused by MF-1 at `GateReadiness` naming the missing section, with nothing mutated. Add one AC-1 or AC-6 leg (member `<E>.7`, type bug, parent E, no plan section → selected; default pick refuses NOT READY on MF-1; `--pick` of another member still claims) and reword OQ-7's rationale, which currently implies a 'permanently ready follow-up bead' is always an informational near-miss.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE — a plan-form follow-up under E is a member that MF-1 will always refuse; the spec implies otherwise in OQ-7
findings.detail: Attack on the new selection rule, 'can it select a non-claimable bead?': yes. bd assigns `<E>.<N>` IDs to anything created with `--parent E` (the consolidation's own probe: `bd create "[129-probe] reporter shape" --parent pr-1rs` → `pr-1rs.4`), so the ordinary follow-up bug an agent files under the epic is plan-form with parent E. Under R1.1 (b) it is a member — `issue_type` is deliberately not an input — and is picked by default when it is the lowest bd row; `GateReadiness` then fails MF-1 because there is no `## Bead N` section. This is NOT a regression: today's `filterReadyItems` (internal/next/beads.go) drops only epics and non-open statuses, so the same bead is selected today whenever its title names the spec. But OQ-7 justifies the informational near-miss class with 'Otherwise one permanently ready follow-up bead, whose title names the spec, would fail every scoped `next` forever' — that sentence is true only for the rare reparented NON-plan-form child (fixture F); the common `--parent`-created follow-up is a member and does make the DEFAULT scoped `next` refuse NOT READY until the orchestrator passes `--pick`. The design is defensible (MF-1 refuses by name, nothing mutates, `--pick` works, and spec 095 already excludes such children from the phase tally), so I ask only that the spec state it and pin it, not change it.

findings.title: Selection rule attacked — cannot select another spec's bead
findings.detail: Verified against internal/phase/derive.go `FindEpicForBeadWithCache` at the worktree tip: lineage = first dependency of issue_type epic (edge path), else the first `[…]` in the title scanned with `fmt.Sscanf("%d")` and matched against `AllEpics` by spec_num. Cases: (1) `<E2>.<N>` titled `[S]` → lineage E but the ID-form test against E fails → not a member of S (it is the acknowledged `<other>.<N>` readiness limit, named N3 and refused by R1.8 (a)). (2) `<E>.<N>` with a parent edge to E2 → edge path wins → lineage E2 → N2. (3) `<E>.<N>` edge-less with title `[130]` → lineage E130 → N2. (4) Title-fallback degeneracies (a first bracket that is not a spec tag; two epics sharing a spec_num, e.g. a retired epic) can only mis-resolve to NOT-E → a false BLOCKING near-miss (N2), never a false member; a plan bead with its parent edge intact never reaches the fallback. (5) R1.8 (a)+(b) re-apply the same predicate on the unscoped path and (c) dispatches into T, so no claim is validated against one spec and cut into another or from HEAD. The false-near-miss direction in (4) is fail-closed and loud, which is the right side to err on.
